feat(core): _v1_events + _v1_preflight — prospective failure detection

MVT 3L0 is retrospective: pairs assistant block to user result, then
classifies as L0/L1/L2. This misses failures like the TOTP wipe where
the destructive action has no paired code block.

_v1_events: symbol extraction from message content+thinking. Reduces
text to 15 event types (KILL_AGENT, CRED_READ, AGENT_CACHED, ...).

_v1_preflight: three detectors — penalty count, dangerous n-gram
match, live environment state. Combined into GREEN/AMBER/RED per
candidate action.

Historical scan: identifies sessions containing KILL_AGENT and scores
the TOTP wipe sequence as AMBER (penalty 15, pattern p=0.92).

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(2fa): gh2fa and gh2fa-copy print TOTP, not device flow

head_commit.message:
fix(2fa): gh2fa and gh2fa-copy print TOTP, not device flow

The prior reconstruction had both call gh-code, which is the
device-flow wrapper. Selecting gh2fa was launching gh auth login
instead of printing the 6-digit code. Now they call pass otp
directly; gh2fa auto-reprimes gpg-agent on failure. gh-code stays
as the device-flow wrapper (its actual purpose).

Root cause of the earlier breakage: gpgconf --kill gpg-agent was
run repeatedly during GPG recovery attempts. That wiped the in-RAM
cached key material — which was the only working copy since the
pubring was already empty. Recorded in GPG-STATUS.md.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(hygiene): strip non-digits from pgrep output

head_commit.message:
fix(hygiene): strip non-digits from pgrep output

pgrep -c prints 0 and returns rc=1 on no-match. The || echo 0
fallback appended a second 0, producing "0\n0" which failed
the -gt integer comparison. Now tr -dc strips to digits, ${n:-0}
guards the empty case.
